newsitem.title: USA: Cold snap causes light damage to Illinois wheat.
newsitem.headline: Cold snap causes light damage to Illinois wheat.

text.p: Illinois soft red winter wheat conditions slipped in the week ended Sunday after record cold temperatures hit the state, the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service reported on Monday.
Wheat was rated two percent very poor, three percent poor, 19 percent fair, 63 percent good and 13 percent excellent. About 79 percent of the crop was rated good to excellent the previous week.
The cold snap virtually halted fieldwork. As of Sunday, two percent of the corn crop had been planted, compared with the five-year average of two percent.
Oats were 63 percent planted, compared with 64 percent last year and the five-year average of 49 percent.
There were 3.1 days suitable for fieldwork.
"Damage to wheat, oats, alfalfa, fruit trees, vegetables and unemerged corn was widespread but only time will tell the severity of the damage," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated four percent short, 72 percent adequate and 24 percent surplus.
Pasture was rated two percent very poor, four percent poor, 28 percent fair, 57 percent good and nine percent excellent.
